spine: 1. Concurrency 必然牽涉取消：兩個非同步計算同時進行時，一方遲早會發現另一方不再需要，必須主動取消它——這不是附加功能，是並行本身的必然結果。
2. 「乾脆開 thread」在取消這件事上撞牆：thread 一旦阻塞在 kernel 的 syscall 裡，語言層 API 通常沒辦法把它叫醒，也沒辦法無限開 thread（系統層限制）。
3. Signal 本身不是可靠的取消機制：signal 天生 racy，可能在 syscall 開始前或結束後才送達，光靠 signal 賭不到正確的時機窗口。

4. Zig 的協定：canceling thread 在 shared memory 設一個 flag，循環對 cancelee 發 signal 直到 acknowledge；被阻塞的 syscall 收到 signal 後回傳 EINTR，thread 檢查 flag 決定 retry 還是 acknowledge 並 unwind——signalCanceledSyscall 與 fileReadPositionalPosix 是這個協定的兩半實作。
5. Windows 有更直接的手段 NtCancelSynchronousIoFile，作者認為 NT 在 fiber、IOCP、Job object 等機制上，並行設計比 Unix 想得更透徹。
6. Prior art 對照：Java 的 thread interrupt 不能真的打斷阻塞中的 syscall；pthread_cancel 有類似的 signal+flag 機制，但不整合語言層的 try/defer 清理，善後麻煩又慢。
7. Zig 的 Io 介面把「可能同時發生」(io.async) 與「必須同時發生」(io.concurrent) 在介面層拆開命名：concurrent 恆可能失敗、async 則不會因此失敗；concurrent 由 thread pool 支撐，池滿才 spawn 新 thread——效果類似 C++ std::launch policy，但顯式命名讓語意更清楚。

perspective.mechanism: 示範一個只用阻塞 syscall、shared-memory flag、與 POSIX signal 就能做到可靠取消的協定，並用 io.async / io.concurrent 的命名把「可能」與「一定」同時發生的兩種並行語意分開。
perspective.tradeoff: 換到的是不必引入 io_uring 或全新的 async runtime、標準阻塞 API 加一個 protocol 就能取消；付出的代價是要自己處理 signal 的競態視窗、EINTR 之後的分支邏輯，以及 signal handler 的限制。
perspective.reader_use: 工程師在自己的框架或 runtime 裡設計 timeout / cancel 機制時，可以拿這個協定當對照組：自己的方案有沒有踩到『signal 本身 racy』或『取消機制不整合語言層清理』這兩個常見坑。

notes.quote: Whenever you have two asynchronous computations happening at the same time, there comes a moment when one computation becomes aware that the second computation is no longer necessary, and must be canceled, actively.
notes.interpretation: 這是 cancelation 存在必要性的核心定義——不是可有可無的附加功能，而是任何兩個生命週期彼此獨立又互相依賴的並行計算，遲早會走到的局面。

notes.quote: the thread is instead blocked inside the syscall in the kernel, programming language APIs generally doesn't give any way to unblock it.
notes.interpretation: 說明「乾脆開 thread」這條路在取消這件事上為什麼撞牆——語言層通常沒有把 kernel 裡的阻塞狀態暴露出來給你操作。

notes.quote: Wouldn't it be cool if we could just use standard OS threads, blocking APIs, avoid new shinies like io_uring, but still get to cancel any work reliably?
notes.interpretation: 作者把整篇文章要解決的問題濃縮成一句話——這是 std.Io.Threaded 存在的動機，用反問句框出目標而非斷言已經達成。

notes.quote: By itself, signals are not a cancelation mechanism — signaling a thread is inherently racy, the signal might get delivered before the relevant syscall starts, or after it finishes.
notes.interpretation: 解釋純 signal 方案為什麼不可靠：時序上無法保證信號送達恰好落在 syscall 正在阻塞的那個窗口內。

notes.quote: the canceling thread sets a flag in shared memory to request cancelation, and then signals the cancelee, in a loop, until the cancelation is acknowledged (a different value for a flag in the shared memory).
notes.interpretation: 這是協定本體：flag 負責傳遞「已經有取消請求」的狀態，signal 只負責把已阻塞的 thread 叫醒去檢查這個 flag，循環直到確認取消為止。

notes.quote: When a thread is blocked in the kernel, and a signal is delivered to the thread, the thread is woken up and the syscall returns EINTR.
notes.interpretation: EINTR 是整個協定能運作的物理基礎——沒有它，signal 送達也沒辦法把執行權交還給使用者態程式碼。

notes.quote: It is customary to just loop re-try the syscall in such cases, but one doesn't have to.
notes.interpretation: 點出 EINTR 之後的分岔點：預設習慣是重試，但取消協定正是利用了「不一定要重試」這個自由度，改成先檢查 flag 再決定。

notes.quote: Upon receiving EINTR from a syscall, the thread potentially being canceled checks the value of the flag and either retries the syscall, or acknowledges the cancelation and begins unwinding.
notes.interpretation: 這是協定的判斷邏輯本體——EINTR 之後的分支正是本文 worked example 要走一遍的核心步驟。

notes.quote: This protocol is implemented in signalCanceledSyscall and fileReadPositionalPosix
notes.interpretation: 指出協定的兩個實作落點：一個負責發 signal / 設 flag 的那一側，一個負責實際阻塞的 syscall 與 EINTR 檢查那一側——原文稱兩者是『the two halves of the protocol』。

notes.quote: On Windows, there's a much more direct NtCancelSynchronousIoFile
notes.interpretation: Windows 不需要 signal+flag 這套間接手段，核心本身就提供直接取消同步 I/O 的 API。

notes.quote: In general, between fibers, IO Completion Ports, Job objects, and this, it seems that NT has a better thought through concurrency story than Unix.
notes.interpretation: 作者對兩個作業系統核心並行設計的價值判斷，用『it seems』明確保留這是個人觀點，不是斷言式定論。

notes.quote: Zig's Io solves this problem ingeniously, separating, at the interface level, 'may run concurrently' from 'must run concurrently'.
notes.interpretation: Io 介面的設計核心——把兩種不同的『同時』語意在命名層面拆開，而不是都塞進同一個『spawn』動作裡。

notes.quote: By naming what is happening (io.async vs io.concurrent), Zig makes it easier to understand what is actually going on, and also gets more precise signatures (concurrent is always fallible, async never is).
notes.interpretation: 具體說明命名拆開後的實際後果：concurrent 因為承諾『一定同時跑』，可能因資源不足而失敗；async 沒有這個承諾，所以不會因此失敗。

notes.quote: This achieves an effect similar to that of std::launch policy (item 36 in effective modern C++, if you have that around).
notes.interpretation: 作者自己把 Zig 的 may/must 拆分類比為 C++ std::launch::async 與 std::launch::deferred 的策略選擇，但用詞是『similar』而非『identical』。

notes.quote: Of course concurrent is backed by a thread pool, falling back on spawning a fresh thread only when the pool is exhausted.
notes.interpretation: must-run-concurrently 的實作細節：預設重用 thread pool，只有池子被榨乾才真的開新 thread——這是為什麼『必須同時』不等於『每次都 spawn』。

notes.quote: In Java, there's a similarly looking thread interruption mechanism. Critically, it doesn't support interrupting syscalls: IOException and InterruptedException are both checked and unrelated, meaning that IOing functions are not interruptible.
notes.interpretation: Java 的 thread interrupt 表面上跟這套協定很像，但關鍵缺陷是它不能真的打斷阻塞在 syscall 裡的 I/O。

notes.quote: pthread_cancel implements a similar signal+flag machinery. However, it doesn't integrate with language-level cancelation (try, defer) which makes post-cancelation cleanup cumbersome and slow.
notes.interpretation: pthread_cancel 已經用了跟 Zig 幾乎一樣的 signal+flag 機制，但沒跟語言層的 try/defer 整合，清理邏輯寫起來麻煩又慢——這正是 Zig 方案要補的那塊。

notes.quote: there are more, the chief being that, while you totally can spawn many threads, this often requires system-wide configuration change, which is a non-starter for most application. But absence of cancelation really makes you hit a wall sooner or later.
notes.interpretation: 解釋「乾脆開更多 thread」為什麼不是萬靈丹：一是系統層限制常需要改設定，多數應用做不到；二是就算 thread 數量夠，沒有取消能力遲早會卡住。

notes.quote: Concurrency is about handling (asynchronous, nondeterministic) events.
notes.interpretation: concurrency 的定義，用來跟下面 parallelism 的定義對照，區分本文談的是哪一種『同時』。

notes.quote: Parallelism is about using hardware resources to do more at the same time.
notes.interpretation: parallelism 的定義，用來跟 concurrency 對照——本文的取消協定談的是 concurrency 那一半，不是 parallelism。
